replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: That's the backbone of the country — enslaved Africans brought by the Dutch, and later contract workers from China, India and Java for the plantations. Javanese Surinamese are still a big part of Suriname today.

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: Dutch is the official language, but on the street you'll hear Sranan Tongo, the creole almost everyone shares. Sarnami Hindustani and Javanese are widely spoken too, along with Maroon and Indigenous languages — a lot of languages for a country of about 600,000.
